title: 2009 AMC 8 Problem 24
statement: The letters \(A,\) \(B,\) \(C\) and \(D\) all represent different digits. If \( \begin{array}{ccc} &A &B \\ + &C &A \\ \hline &D &A \end{array} \) and \( \begin{array}{ccc} &A &B \\ - &C &A \\ \hline &&A \end{array}, \) what digit does \(D\) represent?

solutions.text:
From the ones column of the addition, \(A+B\) ends in \(A,\) so \(B=0.\)

In the subtraction \(AB-CA=A,\) we now have \(A0-CA=A.\) The ones column requires a borrow, so \(10-A=A,\) giving \(A=5.\)

Then \(50-C5=5,\) so \(C=4.\) In the addition, \(50+45=95,\) so \(D=9.\)

Thus, E is the correct answer.
hints: Use the ones column of the addition first.
The subtraction forces a borrowing relation involving \(A.\)
